topics.topic: Whether the exchange directory has an aggregate size limit or only a per-file EFBIG limit
questions: Must the exchange directory have an aggregate bound, or must the reference to an "over-limit exchange directory" be removed so only the per-file EFBIG limit remains?
Must the exchange directory have an aggregate limit, or must references to an “over-limit exchange directory” be removed so only the per-file EFBIG limit remains?

quotes: one fresh private exchange directory bound read-write in which every file the code writes is bounded by the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SANDBOX_SCRATCH_BYTES_MAX constant through the runner's setrlimit file-size limit (the runner ignores SIGXFSZ, so a write past it raises OSError with errno EFBIG), the directory as a whole having no separate bound

A memory, scratch or output bound counts as hit only when the parent observes it from outside: the environment was killed for it, a MemoryError or an OSError for a full or over-limit exchange directory (EFBIG for a file past the file-size limit included) escaped run and reached the parent through the exchange channel, or the output count exceeds bounds.output_bytes
judgement.why: One passage denies any directory-wide bound while the other treats an over-limit exchange directory as a possible scratch-bound event.
